answers.value: The legal rule specifies the twelve latest monthly index observations published in the penultimate month before revaluation. The pinned sources do not establish the publication date of each monthly observation, so the observation window cannot be identified from them. The INSEE metadata identifies an all-items (COICOP 00), total (_T), unadjusted series, but does not establish that this series is the ex-tobacco series required by L.161-25.

"TPH_CPI": "Total",

steps: L.161-25 links the selected monthly observations to their publication by the penultimate month; this is a publication-date condition.
The allowed source set gives observation months and general series metadata, but no publication dates for the monthly observations; therefore it does not substantiate the observation window.
The series metadata says all-items and total, not hors tabac. Do not treat it as proof of the legally named ex-tobacco series.

answers.value: The allowed sources do not establish that the first-quintile ex-tobacco index can replace the index legally named in L.161-25, nor do they establish either index as the legal input to the 2026 SMIC increase. L.161-25 names consumer prices excluding tobacco; the INSEE series metadata separately labels a first-quintile, ex-tobacco series, while the pinned SMIC arrêté states the resulting hourly amount only.

answers.value: DSS/2B/2025/38 states that the family-benefit amounts used to liquidate benefits from 2025-04-01 are rounded to the nearest euro cent. This expressly includes allocations familiales in the listed prestations. It gives an effective start date, not an explicit end date. Thus 2026-03-01 is after its stated start and before the next instruction’s stated start on 2026-04-01; the source text itself does not expressly say “through 2026-03-31.”

citations.paragraph: Metropolitan AF amount by family, two children
citations.quote: 2 enfants          32 %          151,8
Date d’application                     1er avril 2026

steps: The facts specify a two-child family at the full-rate band; D. 521-1 sets 32% of BMAF for the second dependent child. No supplements or differential are included.
The pinned 2025 instruction gives BMAF 474.37 EUR from 2025-04-01. Raw exact product: 474.37 × 32/100 = 151.7984 EUR.

The same instruction says the family-benefit amounts used for liquidation are before CRDS precompte and rounded to the nearest centime. Therefore 151.7984 EUR rounds to 151.80 EUR gross monthly AF before CRDS.

Date scope: DSS/2B/2025/38 states application from 2025-04-01 without an express end date; DSS/2B/2026/46 states its application date is 2026-04-01. Thus 2026-03-01 falls after the 2025 start and before the 2026 stated start, with no explicit 2025 end date in these quoted passages.
This is the statutory gross amount before CRDS; it does not establish whether a payment was actually executed.
